raw_text:
Introduction:
HDFS (Hadoop Distributed File System) is a distributed storage system designed to
handle very large datasets across multiple machines. It is a core component of Hadoop
and is built for scalability, fault tolerance, and high throughput.
Architecture Overview:
HDFS follows a master-slave architecture, where one main node controls the system
and several worker nodes store data.
• The NameNode acts as the master.
• The DataNodes act as slaves.
The NameNode is responsible for managing metadata such as file names, permissions,
and block locations. It does not store actual data but keeps track of where each block is
stored in the cluster.
On the other hand, DataNodes are responsible for storing the actual data. Files are
divided into large blocks (usually 128MB), and these blocks are distributed across
different DataNodes.
Working Process:
When a client wants to read or write a file, it first contacts the NameNode to get
metadata information. After that, the client directly communicates with DataNodes to
perform operations. This reduces load on the NameNode and improves performance.
Key Features of HDFS Architecture:
• Block Storage: Files are split into blocks and stored across nodes.
• Replication: Each block is stored multiple times (default is 3).
• Fault Tolerance: If one node fails, data is still available from other nodes.
HDFS also uses a heartbeat mechanism, where DataNodes regularly send signals to
the NameNode. If a heartbeat is missing, the NameNode assumes the node has failed.
Additional Components:
The Secondary NameNode helps in managing metadata by periodically merging log
files. It is not a backup but supports the main NameNode.
Conclusion:
Overall, HDFS architecture is highly reliable and scalable. It is designed to store
massive data efficiently while ensuring fault tolerance and data availability.

raw_text:
Introduction:
Replication is one of the most important features of HDFS. It ensures that data is not
lost and is always available, even in case of failures.
Why Replication is Important:
In HDFS, each data block is stored multiple times across different DataNodes. The
default replication factor is 3.
This means:
• Each block has three copies
• Stored in different machines (and sometimes racks)
Replication provides several benefits:
• Fault Tolerance: If one node fails, data is still available
• High Availability: Users can access data anytime
• Improved Performance: Multiple copies allow parallel access
Failure Handling in HDFS:
HDFS uses a heartbeat mechanism to detect failures. DataNodes send regular
heartbeat signals to the NameNode.
If a DataNode fails:
• NameNode stops receiving heartbeat
• It marks the node as dead
After detecting failure, the NameNode checks which blocks have lost replicas.
Then:
• It identifies under-replicated blocks
• Creates new copies on other DataNodes
This process is automatic and ensures that the replication factor is maintained.
Data Access During Failure:
Clients are automatically redirected to other available replicas. So even if one node
fails, users can still access data without interruption.
Conclusion:
Thus, replication ensures reliability, fault tolerance, and continuous availability of data
in HDFS. It is a critical feature for handling large-scale distributed systems.

Introduction:
HDFS is a file system used in Hadoop to store large amounts of data across many
computers. It is designed for Big Data applications.
Architecture:
HDFS has two main parts:
• NameNode → manages the system
• DataNodes → store the actual data
The NameNode keeps track of file information and where data is stored. DataNodes
store the data in the form of blocks.
Files are divided into blocks and distributed across different machines. This helps in
storing large files efficiently.
How it works:
When a user wants to access a file, the request goes to the NameNode first. Then the
client directly interacts with DataNodes to read or write data.
Important Features:
• Data is stored in blocks
• Multiple copies are stored (replication)
• System is fault-tolerant
DataNodes send heartbeat signals to NameNode. If a node fails, the system identifies it
and handles the failure.
Conclusion:
HDFS architecture helps in storing and processing large data efficiently and safely.

safety.
Importance:

This helps in:
• Protecting data from failure
• Providing backup copies
• Improving access speed
When DataNode Fails:
DataNodes send heartbeat signals to NameNode.
If a node fails, heartbeat stops.
Then:
• NameNode detects failure
• It creates new copies of data
• Stores them in other nodes
Users can still access data from other copies.
Conclusion:
Replication ensures that data is safe and always available.
